column2: builds it's read otherwise in: all, default (without image-ends) or image-ends
column3: why pdf-content-streams reads it otherwise than PDFium
An operand nested past the 64 levels PDFium reads is an error here, which stops reading, where PDFium reads it as no object and reads on.
An operand nested past the 64 levels PDFium reads is an error here, which stops reading, where PDFium drops what's that deep and reads on.

A JPEG cut short in its coded data: PDFium's decoder (libjpeg-turbo) decodes the content after it as the rest of its rows and stops at the bits its last row needed, an `EI` after it. With image-ends, zune-jpeg reads on to the marker after the coded data, here the content's end, so no `EI` comes after its end and the data is read on from its start with no stream; without it, the stand-in, finding no end of image, ends it at the first `EI` between white-space.

A JPEG with no end of image: PDFium's decoder (libjpeg-turbo) stops at the bits its last row needed and the bytes it read ahead for them, past the first `EI`. With image-ends, zune-jpeg reads on to the marker after the coded data, here the content's end, so no `EI` comes after its end and the data is read on from its start with no stream; without it, the stand-in, finding no end of image, ends it at the first `EI` between white-space.
As dct-no-eoi, with more than 512 bytes of content after it, which puts PDFium's decoder on its fast path, which reads ahead otherwise, here to the same end.

A JPEG of 12-bit samples, which PDFium's decoder (libjpeg-turbo) reads and zune-jpeg doesn't: its header refused, the data is read on from its start with no stream. The stand-in, without image-ends, ends it at its end of image, as PDFium.

Group 4 data cut short: PDFium's decoder decodes the content after it as the rest of its rows, past the first `EI`; with image-ends, hayro-ccitt finds a code that isn't one there and stops, and the end is the stand-in's, the first `EI` between white-space, as without it.

Group 4 data with a byte of its codes changed: PDFium's decoder reads on through what's no code as it can and stops before its last byte; with image-ends, hayro-ccitt can't decode it, and the end is the stand-in's, before the white-space before `EI`, its last byte (0x80, which PDFium reads as white-space) in the data, as without it.

A JPEG of one scan whose last bits its decoder's reader holds before it runs into the end of image: PDFium's decoder (libjpeg-turbo, whose reader takes as many as 64 bits ahead as it needs them) stops short of the end of image, so the `EI` straight after it is no word of its own and the image runs on to the next `EI`. Decoded, zune-jpeg says nothing of where its last row's bits end, so the end is past the marker after them, where libjpeg-turbo's reader stops when it runs into it; the stand-in ends the data at its end of image too; and both end the image at the `EI` straight after.

A JPEG whose metadata holds a thumbnail, its own end of image before the JPEG's, and then a comment holding `EI`: the stand-in ends the data at the thumbnail's end of image and the image at that `EI`, where PDFium's decoder reads past both to the JPEG's end.
A JPEG narrower than the image's /W, which PDFium's decoder refuses: no stream, the data read on from its start. The stand-in ends it at its end of image.
A JPEG cut short in its header, which PDFium's decoder refuses. The stand-in ends it at the first `EI` between white-space.
JPEG data with no start of image, which PDFium's decoder refuses. The stand-in ends it at its end of image.
JPEG data of a start of image alone, which PDFium's decoder refuses. The stand-in ends it at the first `EI` between white-space.

Bytes before the JPEG's start of image: PDFium counts where its decoder stops from the start of image, and adds it to the data's start, so its end falls as many bytes short, here before an `EI` in those bytes. The stand-in ends it at its end of image.

`EI` straight after the fax data, with no white-space before it: PDFium's decoder ends the data at its last row, and the image at that `EI`; the stand-in's `EI` needs white-space before it, and so it takes the next.

Group 4 data with an end of block after its rows, which PDFium's decoder doesn't read, its rows counted: the stand-in ends the data before the white-space before `EI`, a byte of the end of block (0x80, which PDFium reads as white-space) in it.

/Rows 1 of four rows written: PDFium's decoder reads one, and the stream runs on over what's after it to the last word before `EI`, the data's last byte, 0x80, white-space to PDFium, left out; the stand-in ends the data before the white-space before `EI`, that byte in it.
/H 2 of four rows written: as ccf-g4-rows-1.
/Columns past 65,535, which PDFium's decoder refuses. The stand-in ends the data at the first `EI` between white-space.

Fax data with no /DecodeParms: PDFium's decoder reads rows 1728 wide, which these codes don't make, and runs into the content's end, so no `EI` comes after and it keeps no stream. The stand-in ends the data at the first `EI` between white-space.
A row whose codes hold `EI` between white-space (a tab and a 0): the stand-in ends the data there, where PDFium's decoder reads it as codes.

A JPEG cut short at the content's end, ` EI ` in a comment in it: PDFium's decoder reads the content's last two bytes as an end of image, which no `EI` comes after, so it keeps no stream and reads on from the data's start, to the comment's `EI`; the stand-in, finding no end of image, ends the data at that `EI`, and keeps a stream.

A JPEG cut short in its coded data at the content's end, the last two bytes no codes of its tables: PDFium's decoder reads them as an end of image, which no `EI` comes after, so it keeps no stream and reads on from the data's start, to the `EI` in its comment; the stand-in, finding no end of image, ends the data at that `EI`, and keeps a stream.

A JPEG cut short in its coded data at the content's end, its last two bytes a marker's: PDFium's decoder reads them as an end of image, which no `EI` comes after, so it keeps no stream and reads on from the data's start, to the `EI` in its comment; the stand-in, finding no end of image, ends the data at that `EI`, and keeps a stream.

A JPEG cut short in its coded data at the content's end, its last two bytes a marker's: PDFium's decoder reads them as an end of image, which no `EI` comes after, so it keeps no stream and reads on from the data's start, to the `EI` in its comment; the stand-in, finding no end of image, ends the data at that `EI`, and keeps a stream.

Fax data with /DecodeParms but no /Columns: PDFium's decoder reads rows 1728 wide, which these codes don't make, and runs into the content's end, so no `EI` comes after and it keeps no stream. The stand-in ends the data at the first `EI` between white-space.

A JPEG of one scan with a comment holding `(` between its scan and its end of image: PDFium's decoder stops past the comment's marker, the first after the coded data, and the walk from there reads `( ... )` as one string, to the `EI` after it; the stand-in ends the data at its end of image, and the image at the `EI` straight after.
As dct-comment-after-scan, with an application segment holding `(` in the comment's place.
As dct-comment-after-scan, with a restart after each block, which PDFium's decoder reads past.

An Object holds a real as an f64, so 1.00000005960464478, just past halfway between two 32-bit floats, reaches the f64 of that half, which rounds to even, 1, and the white point holds; PDFium parses the bytes straight to a 32-bit float, the one above 1, and it doesn't. So an image in an array of it is 1 component here and 3 there.

A stream whose filter no reader takes, before one that's plain: PDFium reads its data as written, so the path in it is drawn; it's joined here as a stream of no data, its place kept and said (`Concat::undecoded`), as a reader through pdf-objects' `Streams` gives decoded data alone.
As contents-undecoded-bogus, the stream alone: PDFium draws the path in its data as written, and nothing is drawn here.
As contents-undecoded-bogus, through Flate over data that isn't Flate's, which PDFium reads as written where its decoder fails.
As contents-undecoded-flate, the stream alone.
As contents-undecoded-bogus, through DCTDecode, an image's filter, which PDFium doesn't decode for content and reads past, its data as written.
As contents-undecoded-dct, the stream alone.
